analyst_focus.topic: Domestic product launches and market share
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts focused on whether the Pulsar overhaul and new 125cc brands can revive domestic growth.
The market tested how much unprecedented inflation can be offset without sacrificing competitiveness.
Demand exceeds supply for Chetak, making capacity and supply-chain execution central to share gains.
Analysts wanted clarity on operational normalisation and the subsidiary's impact on consolidated performance.
Questions assessed export momentum and the expansion path for Triumph, KTM and commercial motorcycles.
Strong free cash flow prompted questions about future dividends, buybacks and desired cash balances.

manufacturer.revenue_growth: Q1 revenue was approximately ₹17,244 crore, its highest quarterly level.
manufacturer.volume_growth: Q1 volumes reached 1.4 million; all major businesses delivered double-digit growth, though disruptions impaired availability by 10%-15%.
manufacturer.demand_outlook: Strong premium motorcycles, EVs and exports; Chetak demand exceeds supply, while MENA remains disrupted.
manufacturer.margin_outlook: Pricing offset roughly half of 4.5% commodity inflation; Q2 faces broader cost pressure, mitigated by currency, scale and cost control.
manufacturer.ebitda_margin: Q1 EBITDA margin was 20.9%, improving 110 bps YoY.

key_risks: Q2 faces full-period inflation across components, electronics, labour, logistics and energy.
International logistics and West Asia disruption remain volatile.
Capacity and supply constraints are limiting Chetak, premium-bike and export availability.
KTM turnaround and Bajaj Mobility consolidation add execution and reporting complexity.
